structured.answer: I'd open an account at פסגות, which the page marks "הזול", and set up a monthly buy of "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". The page says that leaves "86,045 ₪" after 10 years, but that's for its own example of 10,000 ₪ now plus 500 a month at 7%, not my numbers.

stuck.where: Amount fields at the top (סכום היום 10,000, הפקדה חודשית 500)
stuck.why: It's plainly the place for my own amount, but I only had screenshots so I couldn't change it. So the 86,045 is the page's example, not my 30,000.
Every fund has a minus next to it. At first it looked like they all lose money. I only went ahead because mine is marked "הבחירה" and has the smallest minus.

stuck.where: Coloured bars in the account list
stuck.why: Orange, yellow, red and grey bars on every row, but the key only shows up after the whole list. I had to scroll back and forth to guess that red is דמי ניהול חשבון.
Leumi is a bank I know and it's second. פסגות is cheaper by about 3,000 ₪, and I've at least heard the name, so I went with the cheap one.

findings.what: Every fund shows a minus % and a minus ₪, so they all look like they lose money. It's scary, and it's not explained right next to the numbers.
The colour key for the cost bars sits at the bottom, after 15 rows of bars, so you keep scrolling back to match colours.
Every bank row repeats the same "לא בחישוב מחיר אחר לצעירים, לחיילים..." note. I end up reading it again each time to find what's different.
The same tags "קרן סל" and "מחזיקה את המניות" (cut off on the left) and "בשנה · שנה אחת" on every fund row.
The 86,045 depends on the page's example amounts (10,000 + 500). It sticks in my head as my number even though it isn't.
Words like נאמן and דמי משמרת are thrown at you with no explanation.
The waterfall chart starts at 79,910, a different number from the 86,045 above, and that confused me.
